history.dynasty: Modern (initiated by Baba Neem Karoli / Neeb Karori Ji Maharaj)
history.summary: Sankat Mochan Temple is a Hanuman temple at Taradevi on the Kalka-Shimla National Highway (NH-22/NH-5), about 5-6 km from Shimla, at an altitude of about 975 metres. The saint Baba Neem Karoli (Neeb Karori Ji Maharaj) came to this spot in 1950 and meditated in the woods for ten days; moved by the place, he wished a Hanuman temple to be built here. His devotees — including the then Governor of Himachal Pradesh and Bhagvan Sahai — took up the task, construction began in 1962, and the temple was consecrated on 21 June 1966. The complex grew from a small shrine to a campus of about 18.8 bighas, with separate shrines for Hanuman (main), Rama and Shiva, a Ganesha temple in South Indian architectural style, a shrine to Baba Neem Karoli, a three-storey building used for langar/prasad hall and marriage ceremonies, a children's park and an Ayurvedic clinic.

name: Sankat Mochan Temple
town_description: Shimla is the capital of Himachal Pradesh and was the summer capital of British India, set in the Shivalik Hills at about 2,200 metres. The town centres on the Ridge and Mall Road, with colonial-era landmarks like Christ Church and the Viceregal Lodge, and is linked to Kalka by the UNESCO-listed Kalka-Shimla toy train. It is Himachal's main hill-station tourist hub, famous for Himalayan views, apple country around it, and a cluster of well-known temples.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavism — Hanuman; modern saint lineage of Neem Karoli Baba)

travel.railway: Shimla Railway Station — about 5.5 km; Shimla Old Bus Stand — about 6.4 km
travel.road: On the Kalka-Shimla National Highway at Taradevi, ~5-6 km from Shimla; taxis, HRTC buses and private vehicles available

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November; Ram Navami, Hanuman Jayanti and Dussehra draw the largest crowds; langar/prasad every Sunday
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:30 AM to 8:00 PM in summer; 7:00 AM to 6:30 PM in winter. No entry fee
